target_customer: Small and mid-sized ecommerce brands that need outsourced fulfillment
problem: Small online sellers could not get fast two-day shipping and inventory visibility without building warehouses, which Amazon had made a customer expectation.
business_model: Per-order and storage fees for fulfillment plus software

founders.name: Dhruv Saxena
founders.background_notes: Described by the company as an ecommerce entrepreneur.

founders.name: Divey Gulati
founders.background_notes: Described by the company as an ecommerce entrepreneur.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a warehouse management system, carrier integrations and physical operations; software was standard but operations at scale was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: A network of fulfillment centers and integrations is costly to copy, but many 3PLs offered similar services and margins were thin.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon's fulfillment offering was the benchmark and Shipwire was a market leader; ShipBob stayed independent and by 2021 raised a 200M round reported to value it over 1 billion dollars.

market_need_then: Amazon had set an expectation of fast shipping, and the company founders saw small ecommerce brands lacked efficient supply chain services.

identity.logo: Refreshed by agency Balkan Brothers with a new color scheme; undated
identity.mascot_or_character: Bobby, the name of its AI assistant; no mascot found for the company itself
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, reassuring, benefit focused, short punchy phrases such as 'Chaos-proof your fulfillment'

branding.brand_signature: The Bob suffix across products such as TrackBob
branding.community_and_virality: Merchant case studies on its site; one analysis page alleges merchant departures, unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Easy name with a consistent suffix across products and wide use among ecommerce brands, but no independent brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: ShipBob grew with the ecommerce boom, raising a reported 17.5 million dollar Series B in 2017, a 40 million dollar Series C in 2018 and a 200 million dollar round in June 2021 widely described as unicorn status, then a reported 100 million dollar round in 2022. It stayed independent but closed warehouses and filed WARN notices in 2024, so it is a large growth company with thin margin logistics pressure.
notes: Series A 4M in May 2016 led by Hyde Park is from one aggregator and unverified. Series D 68M in 2020 led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and a 100M Series F in May 2022 at 2.01B post money are single aggregator entries and unverified. The 2021 round is called Series E; the unicorn valuation of about 1B is described as common but not a stated figure so post money is null. Total raised estimates range from 330M to 551M. The competitor search found only current comparisons, nothing dated near 2014, so the list is empty. 2024 WARN notices include Cicero IL and Grapevine TX with conflicting counts. The Series C 2018 date and 40M amount are confirmed by company blog and FreightWaves.
